rationale:
Evidence. The best raced design is iteration 5 (score 160.41): kp 2.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.3, sensor_size 0.016, weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], line_loss search_right. Every race since iteration 2 has ended off_track, with max_error at 0.060 to 0.063 m against the 0.06 m limit.

The approved entityR1 is stale. Its feedback treats ki 0.10 as an untested candidate, but iteration 8 already raced exactly that change and scored 109.75. Oval max_error rose from 0.0604 to 0.0616, progress fell from 0.667 to 0.484, and the oval finish rate dropped from 3/20 to 0/20. The s-bend and slalom were unchanged. The pre-agreed rule therefore applies: revert ki to 0.05 and stop changing gains. Steering gain (kp 3.0, iteration 4), kd (0.45, iteration 6), line-loss direction (search_right and search_left, iterations 5 and 7) and integral gain (ki 0.10, iteration 8) have all been tested and do not improve on iteration 5.

Change. I return to the iteration 5 design unchanged. This is the only candidate with a verified score above 160, and it has completed runs on the oval.

Expected result. About 160 on the development tracks, matching iteration 5 (oval max_error 0.0604, s-bend 0.0623, slalom 0.0616). The next lever is geometry, not gain. If max_error is still about 0.06 m, the next single change should be the outer sensor spacing (x = plus or minus 0.020 m), since sensor_size is at its maximum.

Measurements wanted per track: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation.
